title: A World for Gazebo: The Same Scenario File Made Into an SDF World, With the Ground, the Walls, the Posts, the Goals and the Robot Where They Belong

questions.question: Why make the Gazebo world from the scenario file?
options: Two copies of a wall will disagree, and the simulators then disagree about something never in dispute

questions.question: A wall from (0,0) to (3,4) became a box of length:
questions.explanation: The length of the segment, the angle of its direction.

questions.question: A grade of 0.1 rising along +x is a pitch of:
questions.explanation: A positive rotation about y turns x downwards.

questions.question: Why is a goal a marker with no collision?
options: It is a place, not a thing, and a robot must be able to drive onto it
questions.explanation: A place is not an obstacle.

questions.question: Why are faults not in the world?
options: They concern what the sensors report, so they belong between the world and the program

questions.question: What hides the mistake of laying every wall along x?
options: Axis aligned walls, which are the common ones
questions.explanation: Test a wall that is neither.
